title: Probing Moiré Strain with Bragg Interferometry in 4DSTEM
content: Moiré materials, formed by stacking atomically thin layers with a slight interlayer twist or lattice mismatch, exhibit emergent electronic and optical properties driven by their local stacking configurations and strain fields. These collective structural reconstructions strongly influence plasmonic, phononic, and excitonic behavior, making precise strain mapping critical for understanding moiré-induced phenomena. While electron microscopy techniques can resolve moiré patterns, capturing strain distributions at the atomic scale remains challenging. Here, we apply Bragg interferometry (BI) [1], an interferometric methodology based on four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4DSTEM) [2], to directly measure interlayer strain fields in twisted bilayers and trilayers [3]. Unlike conventional dark field imaging, BI leverages precise virtual apertures to isolate overlapping Bragg disk intensities, allowing us to measure strain from bilayer and trilayer films which are resting on a crystal substrate or even fully encapsulated, both of which generate additional diffraction features.
